## The question

**Do a city's students, academics, and inventors in synthetic biology work on the same things?**

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="58%"}
- Biology moved from *reading* life to *writing* it
- Innovation is local: places branch into related work
- iGEM is a rare open, geotagged record of students learning the field
- We put three artifact types in one semantic space and test for shared topics, city by city
:::
::: {.column width="42%"}
**Three artifact types**

🧬 iGEM projects — 4,606

📄 Academic papers — 10,319

📋 USPTO patents — 2,901

**17,826 artifacts · 80 topics**
:::
:::

::: {.callout-note}
We test semantic relatedness and co-location, not causation.
:::

---

## Why iGEM and BioBricks

- iGEM: a worldwide student competition, projects built from a shared kit of standard DNA parts
- ~89,000 BioBricks in an open registry, each with a stable `BBa_` id and a functional class
- LEGO logic: a part from Uppsala combines with a part from Auckland
- The parts are a second, independent record of what students actually built

> Uppsala 2009's *Booze Bugs* engineered cyanobacteria to make alcohol from sunlight; a 2014 paper cites the team's own BioBrick. One thread, competition to publication.

---

## Building the corpus

| Source | Records | Geocoded to |
|---|--:|---|
| OpenAlex (keyword) | 10,319 papers | institution city |
| Oldham USPTO set | 2,901 patents | inventor cities (fractional) |
| iGEM Registry + wikis | 4,606 projects | team city (multi-tier) |

- Shared schema: id · type · title · text · year · city · country · carbon-capture flag
- Fine-tuned SPECTER2 on ~100k cross-type links (wiki DOIs + Marx patent–paper pairs)
- UMAP → HDBSCAN → 80 human-reviewed topic clusters

---

## The measure that failed

Average a city's projects and papers into two vectors, take the cosine.

- Looks great: similarity ≈ 0.95 almost everywhere
- But it correlates ~0.71 with city size → **centroid collapse**
- It measures *how much* a city publishes, not *what* it publishes

A useful negative result: the fix is to stop averaging and count topics.

---

## The measure that worked

Represent each city as a profile over the 80 topics. Read the cosine overlap of two types, then test it against a **within-country permutation null** (shuffle which city pairs with which, holding size and topic popularity fixed).

| Pair | Cities | Excess | *p* | Beats null? |
|---|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| Project × paper | 120 | +0.0102 | 0.0077 | ✅ |
| Paper × patent | 44 | +0.0352 | 0.0055 | ✅ |
| Project × patent | 28 | +0.0041 | 0.24 | ❌ |

**Papers are the hub. The field is a star, not a triangle.**

---

## Trying to break it

- **Drop any country** — result barely moves (drop US: paper×patent *p* = 0.001)
- **Change cluster count** — project×paper and paper×patent significant across the whole k-sweep; project×patent never
- **Vary the depth threshold** — excess persists, cleaner in deeper cities
- **Base vs fine-tuned model** — survives on base SPECTER2; fine-tuning sharpens, does not invent

---

## The parts agree (Mantel)

Is it all just an artifact of how SPECTER2 reads text? Check the semantic structure against something the model never saw.

- Build a city-by-city distance matrix from the mix of **BioBrick part classes**
- Compare it to the semantic topic-distance matrix
- $r_M = 0.127$, $p = 0.0005$ across 164 cities

Two independent windows, one made of words and one of DNA parts, see the same shape. The strongest single piece of evidence the relatedness is real.

---

## A dynamic trace

Difference-in-differences, within a city and topic, after differencing out each city's baseline and each topic's trend:

- **Paper → patent:** $\hat\beta = +0.355$, $p = 0.028$ ($N = 44$) — academic output predicts later patenting in the same topic
- **Project → paper:** significant in the larger bipartite sample ($N = 161$), underpowered in the tripartite one
- Lead-lag ordering: a null at this sample size (bipartite found a +3-year peak)

---

## Case study: carbon capture

Three adjacent clusters trace the ladder:

- **Cluster 7** Cyanobacterial Metabolic Engineering — projects
- **Cluster 8** Cyanobacterial Chassis Development — papers
- **Cluster 62** Industrial Fermentation — patents

Leaderboard: **Auckland (19), Uppsala (18), Daejeon (15), San Diego (14), Gainesville (13)** — where students, academics, and inventors all work on engineering cyanobacteria at once.

Alignment inside the subfield is as strong as field-wide ($\bar\delta = +0.0140$, 90% positive).

---

## What it shows, and what it can't

**Establishes:** real, size-independent local relatedness between a city's projects and papers, and papers and patents; robust to country, cluster count, threshold, and model; anchored in physical parts.

**Does not establish:** causation. The three share many local causes — same universities, mentors, funders. We document the pattern; we do not identify the mechanism.

**Policy:** where students cluster is a signal of where a field is putting down roots. Funding student science and open tools is an early investment in the field.
